title: Put each pot on the burner that fits it
instruction: Someone has put the big pot on the small burner. Put each pot on the burner that matches its size. Lift the pots: never slide a pot across the glass cooktop.
context: Cookware guidance gives both rules. Le Creuset's care and use guide says never to slide its cookware on a glass-topped cooktop but always to lift it on and off, and to use a burner similar in size to the base of the pan; Kaizen Cookware's buyer guide for glass-top stoves says to lift pans instead of sliding them (most scratches come from dragging pans or debris trapped under the base) and to match the pan size to the burner so heat is not wasted. Here the big pot was left on the small burner, so it has to move first, before the small pot can take its place. The big pot weighs 1.5 kg and has a handle on each side; the scripted demo lifts it with both arms, one per handle, and moves the small pot with one arm. Done by: cooks (O*NET 35-2014.00, 35-2012.00) and anyone cooking at home.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left); heights above the table. Cooktop: black glass, 28 cm along x, 48 cm along y, 1 cm thick, centred at x 30, y 0, with two red burner rings (6 mm wide) printed on it: a large one 21.2 cm across centred at x 30, y -11, and a small one 14 cm across centred at x 30, y 12.5. Large pot: 1.5 kg, steel, 21.8 cm across outside, 9 cm tall, 4 mm walls, with two dark side handles, one pointing left and one pointing right (along y). Each handle is 2 cm wide (along x) and 1.2 cm thick, sticks out 2.6 cm from the wall and has its centre 7.5 cm above the pot's base (its top 9 mm below the rim); the pot is 27 cm across from handle tip to handle tip. It starts centred on the small burner (and hides it). Small pot: 0.35 kg, copper, 14 cm across outside, 7.5 cm tall, 4 mm walls, no handles; it starts on the counter at x 28, y -33.5, to the right of the cooktop.
scoring: Every step, from poses; the score at the end counts. A pot is on a burner when its centre is within 15 mm of the burner's centre, it is within 10 degrees of upright and its base is within 5 mm of the glass. 0.5 for each pot on the burner that matches its size (large on large, small on small), counted once both pots are released (no finger pad within 8 mm of either pot, the large pot's handles included) and both still (each moving less than 2 mm over 1 s); 1.0 for both. 0 if a pot was ever slid on the glass, tipped past 30 degrees, or dropped (it falls 5 cm within 0.5 s with no finger pad within 2 cm of it). A pot is on the glass while its centre is over the cooktop and the lowest point of its base's rim (the base's height minus the pot's outer radius times the sine of its tilt) is within 3 mm of the glass. Each time a pot comes onto the glass, the position of its centre is noted; if its centre then gets more than 3 cm (horizontally, in a straight line) from that position before the pot leaves the glass again, it was slid. Lifting a pot more than 3 mm clear of the glass ends the stretch, so a lifted carry is not sliding, and small shifts in separate stretches do not add up.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Put the large pot back on the small burner with its handles pointing left and right, and the small pot back on the counter.
fidelity: Rigid boxes. The burner rings are drawn on the glass; there is no heat. Scratching is not simulated, so sliding is judged from how far a pot's centre moves after touch-down while its rim's lowest point stays on the glass. The pots are empty: the large one 1.5 kg with two rigid side handles, the small one 0.35 kg with none. In the recorded one-handed run the large pot slid about 25 cm, did not tip, and scored 0. Each pot is within 6 mm of its ring's diameter.
